issues.legal_issue: A contract is not void for mutual mistake of fact when the parties knew the material facts and any mistake concerned their legal effect.
material_facts: The parties knew that the existing lessee had assigned its interest without the lessor’s consent.
The parties knew that the lease made an unauthorised assignment a ground for forfeiture.

The parties proceeded on the understanding that the Government could forfeit the earlier lease and grant a new one; the later decision established that the forfeiture had not legally taken effect because of the law governing registration.
The Government retained title to the property, although the earlier lease restricted its ability to grant a new lease while that lease remained in force.
issues.conclusion: The contract was not void under section 20 of the Indian Contract Act. The parties were not mistaken about essential facts; any mistake concerned the legal effect of the assignment, and under section 21 a mistake of law did not make the contract void.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 20 and 21 of the Indian Contract Act, a mutual mistake of fact concerning an essential matter may void a contract, but a mistake about the legal effect of known facts does not. The Court distinguished Edward H. Cooper v. William Phibbs, where the parties mistakenly believed that one party owned property when the other was in fact entitled to it.

predicates.contract_validity_dispute: The dispute concerns whether an agreement is invalid because the parties made a mistake.
predicates.parties_knew_material_facts: Both parties knew the underlying facts on which the agreement proceeded.
predicates.mistake_concerned_legal_effect: Any error concerned the legal effect of known facts rather than the facts themselves.

issues.definition: When a contract-validity dispute concerns parties who knew the material facts but misunderstood their legal effect, the contract is not void for mistake.

issues.legal_issue: A party that denied the existence of a contract without pleading its legal unenforceability cannot raise a new, fact-dependent objection to enforceability for the first time in argument when the opposing party lacked an opportunity to meet it.
material_facts: The Government’s pleadings disputed whether a concluded contract had been made but did not plead that the contract was unenforceable for failure to comply with the required manner of execution.
The objection was raised for the first time during argument in the High Court.
Determining whether the Government’s authorised officer had signed the relevant lease documents required factual investigation.
The company had sought production of the documents, but the Government did not produce all of them, and the company had no opportunity at trial to present evidence addressing the objection.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have allowed the objection to be raised at the argument stage. The Court rejected the objection on that procedural ground without deciding whether the contract had in fact been executed in the required manner.
issues.legal_principle: Order VI, rule 8 of the Civil Procedure Code provides that a bare denial of an alleged contract is a denial of fact, not a denial of its legality or legal sufficiency. Order VIII, rule 2 requires a defendant to plead matters showing that a transaction is void or unenforceable, including grounds that would take the other party by surprise or raise factual issues not arising from the plaint.

rule.if: contract_enforcement_suit and contract_denied_only_as_a_fact and unenforceability_not_pleaded and defense_requires_factual_inquiry and opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_meet_defense

predicates.contract_enforcement_suit: A claimant seeks enforcement of an alleged contract.
predicates.contract_denied_only_as_a_fact: The opposing party’s pleadings deny that the contract was made but do not challenge its legal enforceability.
predicates.unenforceability_not_pleaded: The opposing party did not plead the legal ground later relied on to resist enforcement.
predicates.defense_requires_factual_inquiry: Deciding the late defense would require investigation of facts.
predicates.opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_mee: The claimant had no adequate opportunity to present evidence or otherwise address the factual defense.

issues.definition: In a contract-enforcement suit, a fact-dependent enforceability defense not pleaded after only a factual denial cannot be raised late when the claimant lacked an opportunity to meet it.

issues.legal_issue: A party that contracts to grant property while its title is restricted by an existing interest may be required to perform once that impediment ends and the contracted-for interest becomes available.
material_facts: The Government agreed to grant leases while an earlier lease over the property remained in force.
The earlier lease prevented the Government from granting the company an immediately effective lease, so the Government had an imperfect rather than wholly absent title for that purpose.
The earlier lease expired, removing the impediment to the Government granting the agreed leases.
The Government resisted the company’s claim and granted leases to another party.
issues.conclusion: Section 18(a) of the Specific Relief Act applied. Once the earlier lease expired, the company’s right to obtain the agreed leases revived, and it was entitled to sue for specific performance, subject to the applicable limits on the relief ultimately available.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18(a) of the Specific Relief Act permits a purchaser or lessee to compel performance from a vendor or lessor who contracted with an imperfect title and later acquired the interest needed to perform. The Court treated an existing lease that temporarily restricted the lessor’s ability to grant the new lease as an imperfection in title, not an absence of title.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and contract_to_grant_property and existing_interest_prevented_immediate_grant and existing_interest_later_expired

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A claimant brings a suit seeking specific performance of a contract to transfer or let property.
predicates.contract_to_grant_property: The parties made a contract under which one party agreed to grant an interest in property.
predicates.existing_interest_prevented_immediate_gr: An existing interest in the property prevented the contracting party from immediately granting the agreed interest.
predicates.existing_interest_later_expired: The existing interest later ended, removing the impediment to grant.

issues.definition: When an existing interest prevents immediate performance of a property-grant contract but later ends, the claimant may seek specific performance of the interest then available.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant may relinquish claims to further performance during litigation to satisfy the condition for seeking performance of the remaining part of a contract.
material_facts: The contract covered a longer lease period, but a substantial part of that period had already passed.
During the litigation, the company sought relief for the remaining period and stated that it relinquished claims to further performance and to compensation for the earlier period.
The company confirmed in argument that it insisted on no further performance and claimed no compensation for the period before performance could be given.
issues.conclusion: The relinquishment was sufficient, and it could be made at any stage of the litigation. The company could therefore seek relief under section 15 of the Specific Relief Act, subject to the Court’s decision on what relief to grant.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15 of the Specific Relief Act permits relief for the performable part of a contract subject to its conditions, including relinquishment of claims to further performance and compensation for the unperformed part. The Court relied on Waryam Singh v. Gopi Chand for the principle that relinquishment of the claim to further performance may be made at any stage of litigation.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A claimant brings a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.substantial_part_of_contract_already_ela: A substantial part of the contract’s performance period has passed before relief is considered.
predicates.claimant_relinquished_claim_to_further_p: During the litigation, the claimant gives up claims to further performance beyond the part for which relief is sought.

issues.definition: When a substantial part of a contract has already elapsed, a claimant in a specific-performance suit may make the required relinquishment during the litigation.

issues.legal_issue: Specific performance may be refused when the remaining performance would yield little practical benefit, while compensation may still be awarded for the period in which performance was unavailable.
material_facts: Only a short portion of the agreed lease period remained by the time the matter was decided.
Carrying on quarrying operations for that short remaining period would scarcely be worthwhile.
The contract did not give the company a right to renewal as a matter of entitlement; renewal depended on agreement on terms and official approval.
The company had claimed compensation, and the Government had prevented it from obtaining possession after the earlier lease expired.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to decree specific performance for the short remaining period but awarded compensation for the period from the expiry of the earlier lease to the end of the agreed lease term, with the amount to be determined by the trial court.
issues.legal_principle: Although the conditions for relief under section 15 of the Specific Relief Act were met, specific performance was refused because the short remaining term would yield no material practical benefit, and renewal was not assured as a matter of right. The Court nevertheless allowed the claim for compensation for the period during which the company was deprived of the contracted-for lease.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and little_time_remained_for_performance and performance_would_yield_little_practical_benefit and no_right_to_renewal and compensation_claimed_for_deprivation

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A claimant brings a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.little_time_remained_for_performance: Only a short portion of the agreed performance period remained when relief was considered.
predicates.performance_would_yield_little_practical: Carrying out the remaining performance would provide little practical benefit.
predicates.no_right_to_renewal: The contract did not give the claimant an enforceable right to renewal as a matter of entitlement.
predicates.compensation_claimed_for_deprivation: The claimant sought compensation for the period in which the promised performance was unavailable.

issues.definition: When little time remains, performance would yield little practical benefit, renewal is not assured as a right, and compensation is claimed for deprivation, specific performance may be refused while compensation is awarded.
